storage: No tables of its own: rows go to core's raw.record (a version only when an order or closure changes) and evt.event (one row per order or closure). About 2 MB holds the Oct 7 set (15 orders and closures, mostly the fire closures' polygons, in both tables); a few changes a month add well under 1 MB a day. Plus 72 ops.fetch rows a day (3 sources, hourly). Download: about 1 MB a day of layer metadata, plus 0.3-1.1 MB per full read (at most hourly after edits, at least daily).
ethics: Query-only reads of public ArcGIS layers (ingest/http.py refuses edit operations); robots.txt at services1.arcgis.com answers 403 (no rules). Order PDFs, alert pages and other links are kept as links and never fetched. Staff user-name fields are dropped; office phone numbers (agency offices, not people) are kept. USFS orders are public domain, but the signed order is the authority, not the polygon. IDPR's terms allow non-commercial use with attribution: internal or published only as aggregates until IDPR gives a licence or a yes, and a courtesy note to IDPR is due (ch. 17 Q17).
